source.name: BBC Science & Environment
source.title: Aviation faces hotter, stormier skies – and passengers might have to accept more disruption
source.summary: Are people going to have to increasingly accept more delays and diversions as the effects of climate change intensify?
source.evidence_text:
The report examines how climate change and more severe weather could increase interruptions to aviation.
Storms near London and across northern Europe caused substantial flight delays during a busy summer travel period.
Air traffic teams tried to guide aircraft around storms, leaving less usable airspace and some departures waiting on the ground.
Poor conditions can require aircraft to take different paths or land at another airport.
An airport receiving diverted aircraft needs room for planes and facilities for additional passengers.
Pilots use weather radar and forecasting information to help avoid dangerous storm conditions.
Storm cells can move quickly, and changes to a flight’s course may occur late in the journey.
Longer flight paths can require more fuel and increase airline costs.
Flooding can affect airport operations and prevent travellers from reaching airports by road or rail.
The report presents future disruption as a risk rather than claiming every flight will be affected.
source.evidence_kind: Editor-written factual notes paraphrased from the linked BBC article; not quotations or independent reporting.
